title: Joining a Community Choir
context: A caller telephones the secretary of a local choir to ask about joining.

script.speaker: Secretary
script.text: Good evening, Riverbank Community Choir, Anna speaking.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Oh, hello. I saw a poster in the library about joining, and I wanted to ask a few questions before I turn up.

script.speaker: Secretary
script.text: Of course. Have you sung in a choir before?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Not since school, so about fifteen years ago. I'm a bit worried I've forgotten everything.

script.speaker: Secretary
script.text: Don't be. We're what's called a non-auditioned choir, which means anyone can join — there's no test at the door. About a third of our members hadn't sung since school either.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: That's reassuring. Do I need to read music?

script.speaker: Secretary
script.text: It helps, but it isn't required. We record each voice part separately and put the files online, so people can learn at home by listening. Quite a lot of our members work that way entirely.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Good. And when do you meet?

script.speaker: Secretary
script.text: Thursdays, seven until nine, in the hall behind Saint Alban's Church. That's on Mill Lane, not the church on the high street — people get those two confused constantly.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Mill Lane. I'll write that down. Is there parking?

script.speaker: Secretary
script.text: There's a small car park but it fills up by about ten to seven. Most people use the multi-storey on Bridge Street and walk across; it's four minutes.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Fine. What about the cost?

script.speaker: Secretary
script.text: The term fee is forty-eight pounds, and that covers ten rehearsals and the sheet music. If you're a student or over sixty-five it's thirty-two. And your first rehearsal is free, so you can come along and see whether you like us before paying anything.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: That's very fair. Do you perform?

script.speaker: Secretary
script.text: Twice a term. The winter concert is always in the church itself, and the summer one has been outdoors in the park for the last few years, weather permitting.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Do I need to buy anything to wear?

script.speaker: Secretary
script.text: Just plain black — trousers or a skirt, and a black top. We provide a scarf in the choir colours, and you give that back if you leave. Please don't buy anything special before your first concert; people always buy the wrong thing.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Understood. One last thing — my daughter is twelve and she sings all the time. Could she come?

script.speaker: Secretary
script.text: Not to the main choir, I'm afraid; the minimum age is sixteen. But we run a youth section on Saturday mornings, ten until half past eleven, and that takes children from eight upwards. Same hall.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Perfect. Who should I speak to about that?

script.speaker: Secretary
script.text: That's Ravi Sharma — I'll give you his email. It's r dot sharma at riverbankchoir dot org.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Got it. And should I bring anything on Thursday?

script.speaker: Secretary
script.text: A bottle of water and a pencil. Everyone forgets the pencil, and you'll want to mark your part.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: A pencil. Right. Thank you very much.

script.speaker: Secretary
script.text: See you Thursday.

questions.instruction: Complete the notes below. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS OR A NUMBER for each answer.

questions.explanation: The secretary says “Thursdays, seven until nine”. The caller confirms at the end with “on Thursday”, so the day is stated twice.

questions.sentence: The hall is behind Saint Alban's Church on ___ Lane.
questions.explanation: “In the hall behind Saint Alban's Church. That's on Mill Lane, not the church on the high street.” The distractor is the high-street church.

questions.sentence: The full term fee is ___ pounds.
questions.explanation: “The term fee is forty-eight pounds.” Thirty-two is the concession rate for students and the over-sixty-fives, so it is the distractor.

questions.sentence: Members must wear plain ___ clothing for concerts.
questions.explanation: “Just plain black — trousers or a skirt, and a black top.” The scarf is supplied by the choir, so it is not what members must wear of their own.

questions.sentence: The minimum age for the main choir is ___.
questions.explanation: “The minimum age is sixteen.” Eight is the minimum for the youth section and twelve is the daughter's age — both are distractors.

questions.sentence: Newcomers are told to bring water and a ___.
questions.explanation: “A bottle of water and a pencil. Everyone forgets the pencil, and you'll want to mark your part.”

questions.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

questions.question: What does the secretary say about musical ability?
options: Applicants must pass a short audition
Anyone may join without being tested
Only former choir members are accepted
questions.explanation: “We're what's called a non-auditioned choir, which means anyone can join — there's no test at the door.”

questions.question: How do many members learn their part?
options: By reading printed sheet music at home
By listening to recordings put online
By attending an extra weekly class
questions.explanation: “We record each voice part separately and put the files online, so people can learn at home by listening.” Reading music “helps, but it isn't required”.

questions.question: What is the caller advised about parking?
options: To arrive before ten to seven for the car park
To use the multi-storey on Bridge Street
To park in the church grounds
questions.explanation: The car park “fills up by about ten to seven”, so “most people use the multi-storey on Bridge Street and walk across”. The advice is the recommendation, not the deadline.

questions.question: Where is the summer concert normally held?
questions.explanation: “The winter concert is always in the church itself, and the summer one has been outdoors in the park for the last few years.”
